title: revocation-http: no URI filtering for SSRF
description:
pkix-revocation-http fetches whatever URIs appear in certificate CDP and AIA extensions (extract.rs). The crate's own rustdoc (lib.rs line 93-96) explicitly documents this as out-of-scope: 'No CDP / AIA URI filtering. This crate fetches whichever URI is in the certificate's CRLDistributionPoints or AuthorityInfoAccess extension. Restrictions on which hosts / schemes are acceptable for revocation fetches (e.g., enforcing HTTPS or blocking private-network URIs) are a deployment-policy decision and stay outside this crate.'

What goes wrong (integrity/availability): A certificate with http://169.254.169.254/... or http://10.0.0.1/... in its AIA/CDP extensions could probe internal networks via SSRF when the library is used in a server-side context. The library correctly filters to http/https schemes only (no file://, ldap://, etc.) but does not filter by destination IP or hostname.

This is documented and intentional -- the delegation to the RevocationFetcher trait is the right architecture. But callers may not realize they need to implement host filtering in their RevocationFetcher. A 'Security Considerations' section in the crate rustdoc would help.

Location: /home/mark/PROJECT/PKIX/pkix-revocation-http/src/lib.rs (documented at lines 93-96)
